pages.text: Rain pattered down. Under the front eaves, Riri spread her raincoat and studied it. "Does this button go in this hole or that one?" She looked between buttons and holes.
Lolo in boots waved from the yard. "Riri, a puddle! Hurry!" "I want to come! Just the buttons first!" Riri turned the coat over, then spread it out again.
Riri counted buttons on her fingers. "One, two, three, four, five." Five holes too. While she chose where to start, rain tapped her shoulders. They grew damp.
Mom opened the door and came out in her blue apron. "Riri, you do not have to choose a button." She picked up the top one.
"Top button into the top hole." Mom fastened the first button. Then the buttons and holes below lined up in pairs. "Oh! Now I can see which is which!"
Riri slipped the second button in, then the third. Beside her, Mom sang, "Buttons from the top—one, two!" Riri's fingers grew quicker.
Fourth, fifth—the last button slipped in. Riri pulled on her yellow hat and shook out her coat. She had fastened them all herself!
Riri walked into the rain. Lolo waved from the puddle. Raindrops rolled off the coat. Inside, it was dry.
The next morning, Riri put on her raincoat without calling Mom. "One, top button first! Two, one by one down! Three, hat on!" All five buttons fastened easily.
Mom lifted Riri and pressed cheek to cheek. "Start at the top, one by one, and there is no need to choose, right?" Smiling over Mom's shoulder, Riri said, "Buttons from the top—one, two!"
